turns.text: I have a 70-year-old female with a 2 cm endometrial cancer (Grade 1, Stage IA) who has severe aortic stenosis (valve area 0.7 cm2, peak gradient 58 mmHg). She is not a surgical candidate due to her cardiac risk. Her cardiologist says she has a 5-year survival of approximately 40% from her cardiac disease. She wants definitive treatment. Should I recommend definitive brachytherapy alone? What fractionation would minimize treatment visits? What anesthesia considerations are important? Should I consider active surveillance given her limited cardiac life expectancy?

A 45-year-old woman with stage IVA cervical cancer completed definitive chemoradiation (EBRT 45 Gy + cisplatin/5-FU + 4 fractions HDR 28 Gy to point A). She now has a 2 cm exophytic vaginal apex recurrence 14 months later. Her renal function recovered after bilateral ureteral stents, ECOG 1. Outline the salvage treatment workflow including restaging, re-irradiation dose constraints, treatment options, and surveillance.
